 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Sunil Kumar Panwar
 Oral Order
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned A.P.P appearing on behalf of the State.
The petitioner is languishing in custody in a case registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 504, 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 138 of the N.I. Act.

The prosecution case as per F.I.R is that informant's company is doing the business of soap,
detergent, noodles, refind oil etc in the entire State of Bihar.

It is further alleged that the informant was not Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.61610 of 2022(3) dt.21-02-2023 well and was undergoing treatment and taking the benefit of the same, the petitioner and other F.I.R named accused persons have fraudulently kept the money and on several request by the staff of the informant, they did not return the money.
The petitioner is alleged to have not paid Rs. 14,38,594/- and the cheque issued by the petitioner was also got bounced.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that petitioner is innocent and he has falsely been implicated in this case.

The petitioner also runes the business and in the year 2012-13, he entered into an agreement with the informant and at that time, the petitioner gave three cheques without signature and date to the informant but the petitioner was not happy with the goods which were supplied and since the goods supplied was not of standard quality, he requested the informant to hand over the aforesaid three cheques.
The said cheques were later on used by the informant as a tool against the petitioner.
The petitioner is languishing Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.61610 of 2022(3) dt.21-02-2023 in custody since 04.01.2022.

Considering the facts aforesaid and the period under custody, let the petitioner, above named, be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs. 10,000/- (Ten Thousands) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Vaishali at Hajipur in connection with Hajipur Industrial P.S. Case No. 174 of 2021.
